results.title: KOGAS wins prime minister's award for helping small businesses go global
results.content: Korea Gas Corp. (KOGAS) has won a prime minister’s citation for turning its industrial expertise into a broader support network for smaller businesses, helping them develop domestic technology, enter overseas markets and reduce financing costs. The state-run energy company said Friday it received the award at the 2026 Shared Growth Week ceremony held at Coex Magok in Seoul on Thursday, recognizing its efforts to promote cooperation between large corporations and small and midsize enterprises. One of its major achievements was helping localize cryogenic ball bearings designed to operate at temperatures as low as minus 162 degrees Celsius, a technology previously dependent on imports. results.title: Overseas card spending hits record high in Q3
results.content: South Koreans' overseas card spending hit the highest-ever amount in the third quarter of the year on the back of an increase in outbound travelers, data showed Friday. The amount of money spent overseas by South Koreans with credit and debit cards came to $6.63 billion in the July-September period, up 13.3 percent from three months earlier, according to data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The on-quarter rise marks the sharpest since the first quarter of 2023, when the reading spiked 14.8 percent, and also is the largest-ever. The central bank said more South Koreans traveled overseas, although direct purchases from abroad declined. The number of overseas travelers came to 7.12 million in the third quarter of the year, up 7.4 percent from the previous quarter. The combined amount of purchases made through overseas shopping malls, on the other hand, fell 0.8 percent to $1.4 billion.

results.title: Pay-TV subscribers continue to decline; IPTV subscribers slightly up in H1: data
results.content: The number of pay-TV subscribers has declined for the past two years, while the number of people using Internet Protocol TV (IPTV) services has maintained a steady uptrend, data from the country's media watchdog showed Friday. The number of people subscribed to pay-TV services in South Korea fell 0.29 percent from the second half of 2025 to 36 million as of June this year, according to findings by the Korea Media and Communications Commission (KMCC). The number has been dropping since the second half of 2024, the KMCC said. In contrast, IPTV service subscribers inched up 0.47 percent from six months earlier to 21.6 million, accounting for over 60 percent of the market, according to the data. By company, KT accounted for the most with 25.39 percent, followed by SK Broadband with 18.67 percent and LG Uplus with 15.96 percent. results.title: Market volatility expanding amid AI uncertainties: financial authorities
results.content: Global stocks are experiencing increasing volatility due to artificial intelligence (AI)-linked uncertainties, and there is a need to guard against the deepening ties between the chipmaking sector's cycle and the financial market, South Korean authorities said Friday. Earlier in the day, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il held a meeting with heads of the Bank of Korea, the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and other related agencies to check market conditions. The policymakers echoed views that the local stock market's volatility is growing due to uncertainties surrounding the AI sector and changes in the global trade environment. In particular, they said it needs to closely check the risks related to the correlation of the chip sector and the stock market. results.title: Ex-President Yoon's senior aide gets suspended prison term over presidential residence relocation
results.content: A Seoul district court on Friday sentenced a former senior aide to former President Yoon Suk Yeol to a suspended prison term over irregularities in the 2022 relocation of the presidential residence. The Seoul Central District Court handed down a two-year prison sentence, suspended for three years, for former presidential chief of staff Kim Dae-ki after finding him guilty of abusing his power in connection with the case. It also sentenced former presidential secretary for administrative affairs Yoon Jae-soon and former presidential secretary for general affairs Kim Oh-jin to one-year prison terms, both suspended for two years. results.title: Lee Jong-suk proves he's still the romance king in 'The Remarried Empress'
results.content: Despite early criticism surrounding Disney+'s fantasy romance series "The Remarried Empress," Lee Jong-suk emerged as one of its biggest winners, winning over viewers with his romantic chemistry with Shin Min-a and reaffirming his reputation as a master of on-screen romance. The 10-episode series concluded with a happy ending as Empress Navier (Shin Min-a), after divorcing Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon), marries Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) and embarks on a new chapter in her love life. Based on the popular web novel and webtoon of the same name, "The Remarried Empress" generated considerable anticipation ahead of its release for bringing romance fantasy, a genre widely popular in Korean digital comics and fiction but relatively uncommon in live-action K-dramas, to the screen. results.title: Korea expands customs tech footprint with Guatemala's launch of UNI-PASS system
results.content: Korea is extending its digital customs network into Central America, with Guatemala launching an electronic clearance system developed through a five-year cooperation project designed to speed up trade and strengthen customs enforcement. The Korea Customs Service said Friday that Guatemala officially opened its upgraded electronic customs system, known as UNI-PASS, at the headquarters of its tax authority, the Superintendency of Tax Administration, in Guatemala City on Thursday (local time). The ceremony was attended by Kim Ki-dong, director-general for information and data policy at the Korea Customs Service, Korean Ambassador to Guatemala Kim Deuk-hwan and Guatemalan tax chief Werner Ovalle, along with officials from both countries. results.title: Sungkyunkwan University ranks 24th worldwide in THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings
results.content: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) ranked 24th worldwide in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027, highlighting its growing strength in interdisciplinary research. SKKU climbed 19 places from last year’s ranking of 43rd to become the top-ranked university in Korea. “This achievement reflects international recognition of our university members’ efforts to tackle societal challenges beyond disciplinary boundaries,” SKKU President Yoo Ji-beom said. “We will continue to advance as a global research-oriented university at the forefront of interdisciplinary research,” he added. A total of 1,058 universities worldwide were ranked in this year’s assessment, released by THE, a U.K.-based higher education ranking organization. results.title: Cadillac launches Korean-designed Vistiq electric SUV in Korea
results.content: Cadillac has launched the Vistiq, an all-electric, three-row large SUV, in Korea. The model's design and engineering were led by GM's research and development arm in the country, the U.S. luxury automaker said Friday. GM Technical Center Korea led the development of the Vistiq, which went on sale first in North America. There, it picked up the nickname "Baby Escalade," after Cadillac's flagship full-size SUV. The Vistiq will be sold in Korea only in the top-end Platinum trim, priced at 181.7 million won after tax benefits for eco-friendly vehicles. The SUV is 5,235 millimeters long and 2,025 millimeters wide, with a 3,094-millimeter wheelbase. It seats six in three rows, with two seats in each row. results.title: N. Korean fishing boat repatriated, with 1 crewman opting to stay in S. Korea
results.content: South Korea sent a North Korean fishing boat back across the sea border Friday with six of its seven crew members aboard as one decided to stay, the unification ministry said. The vessel, found near Ulleung Island in the East Sea earlier this month, crossed the Northern Limit Line (NLL), the de facto maritime border, at 8:33 a.m. and met a North Korean ship waiting on the other side at 9 a.m., the ministry said. The boat was found adrift Nov. 3 in international waters north of the South Korean island. Of the seven North Koreans aboard, one expressed a wish to stay in the South. The ministry decided to repatriate the six crewmen on humanitarian grounds. The remaining one will be protected in South Korea as a defector under relevant laws. results.title: From metal type to AI: Korea's reading culture to be explored at MMCA
results.content: In an age of endless scrolling and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated text, why does reading still matter? The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA), Korea, poses that question in "Ways of Reading," which opens on Friday at its Seoul branch. The exhibition retells the history of Korean graphic design and publishing since the 1970s through the everyday act of reading. The show will run through April 11 next year, featuring about 500 works and materials by roughly 40 teams. "Amid the flood of images that envelops us, this exhibition asks why reading remains valid," MMCA Director Ki Hye-kyung said during a press preview Thursday. She noted that the ongoing "text-hip" trend, in which young people share passages from books and images of themselves reading on social media, is itself "another facet of image culture built on reading." results.title: Korea's speed, Finland's lifelong learning could build human skills in AI age
results.content: As concerns mount over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating in examinations, educators and experts are calling for a fundamental rethink of how students are taught and assessed in the age of AI. The issue was a central topic at the Korea-Finland Innovation Forum 2026, held Wednesday at Korea University's SK Future Hall. Under the theme "Human Capabilities in the AI Age," academics, government officials and industry representatives explored how education must move beyond memorization to developing creativity and critical thinking. Welcoming participants, Finnish Ambassador to Korea Jyri Järviaho said AI would have a profound impact on future jobs and the skills required to perform them, making it essential for education systems to adapt to changing realities. results.title: Korea boosts commuter bus accessibility for people with disabilities
results.content: More than half of Korea’s city buses now feature low-floor designs, marking a significant step toward making public transportation more accessible to an aging population and people with mobility challenges. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said Friday that low-floor buses accounted for 51.8 percent of the nation’s city bus fleet in 2025, with 18,160 vehicles in operation. That represents an increase of 2,417 buses from the previous year, bringing the country past the 50 percent milestone. The progress comes as demand for accessible transportation continues to grow. According to the ministry’s 2025 transportation accessibility survey, 16.46 million people, or 32.2 percent of Korea’s population, were classified as having mobility challenges at the end of last year, up approximately 330,000 from 2024. results.title: Korea Tourism Organization, ROK-US Command join forces to boost cultural tourism
results.content: The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) and the United States Forces Korea (USFK) are strengthening ties through a new partnership aimed at expanding cultural exchange and promoting regional tourism across Korea. The KTO said Friday that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with the ROK-US Combined Forces Command to promote tourism and cultural exchange as part of efforts to deepen friendship between the two countries. Building on the success of joint tourism and cultural experience programs conducted this year, the agreement aims to provide U.S. and Korean military personnel and their families with more opportunities to explore Korean culture while encouraging visits to destinations beyond major cities. results.title: HUFS to build 1st inter-university dormitory among private universities
results.content: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies (HUFS) signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Advancing Schools Foundation on Monday to build an inter-university dormitory and improve its educational facilities. The agreement was signed by HUFS President Kang Kee-hoon and Lee Ha-woon, chairman of the foundation, at HUFS’ Seoul campus, the university said. The two institutions have agreed to build a privately funded Haengbok (Happy) Dormitory that will accommodate students from HUFS and nearby universities in Seoul, while improving the university’s educational environment and promoting sustainable development. The project is the first of its kind to be undertaken by a private university in Korea, HUFS said. results.title: CSAT perfect scorers shun spotlight amid AI cheating suspicions
results.content: At least three students are believed to have earned perfect scores on this year's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), yet they are shunning the spotlight for fear of being suspected of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating. The current tally of three is based on preliminary self-grading, with the number expected to rise when official results are released on Dec. 11. High schools and private academies have long been eager to publicize perfect scorers on Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam, with news of such achievements emerging as early as exam day last year. Their study habits, daily routines and university aspirations have often made headlines, while schools have celebrated their success as a source of pride. results.title: K-art takes center stage in Seoul with new wave of young talent
results.content: A new exhibition in central Seoul is betting that Korea’s next cultural export may come not from a music stage or television screen, but from the studios of its emerging contemporary artists. The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) is opening “NEW WAVE,” a special exhibition showcasing works by 10 promising Korean artists, at HiKR Ground, its tourism promotion center in Jung District, Seoul, Friday. Running through March 30, 2027, the exhibition is being organized in partnership with the Galleries Association of Korea and will offer free admission at the center’s fourth-floor Local Ground gallery. The exhibition, themed “A new wave: Young artists to watch now,” will unfold in two group shows, each featuring five artists. results.title: Data reveals how medical tourists explore Korea beyond hospitals
results.content: Korea is looking to turn its booming medical tourism industry into a wider driver of regional tourism, using big data to understand where international patients travel, shop and spend beyond their hospital visits. The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO), in partnership with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, hosted the third Korea Tourism Today Data Seminar at Coex in southern Seoul this week. Bringing together around 500 representatives from local governments, the tourism industry and academia, the event explored the current landscape and future growth potential of K-medical tourism through mobility and consumption data. The seminar presented an analysis of medical tourism spending across six major regions: Seoul, Busan, Daegu, Jeju, Gyeonggi Province and Incheon. results.content: Actor Song Joong-ki is drawing attention for his remarkably youthful appearance, with a recent firsthand account suggesting that the father of two seems to have barely aged. results.content: A North Korean defector has been taken into police custody after entering a civilian restricted area near the inter-Korean border and is currently undergoing questioning, a military official said Friday. The military found the woman in her 30s at around 6:40 p.m. Thursday between a village north of the Civilian Control Line (CCL) and the general outpost fence in the border county of Cheorwon, about 75 kilometers northeast of Seoul, a Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) official said. Police and relevant authorities are questioning her over possible espionage linked to North Korea, among other suspicions, the JCS official said. results.title: Renault Filante targets drivers sensitive to ride comfort
results.content: For some drivers, ride comfort is decided by the smallest details — a bump over a speed hump, a manhole cover or a seam in the road. These minor impacts may go unnoticed at first, but once drivers become sensitive to them, they can become a constant part of the driving experience. Unlike horsepower or fuel economy, ride comfort is difficult to capture in a specification sheet. It depends on how a vehicle responds to different road surfaces and how effectively it keeps vibrations and noise away from occupants. Renault Korea’s flagship Filante crossover is designed around this everyday driving experience, with a focus on balancing comfort and stability across a wide range of road conditions. A key part of the setup is its frequency-sensitive damper, which is fitted as standard across the lineup. results.title: Lee's approval rating rises for 2nd straight week: poll
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating rose for the second consecutive week to 41 percent, a poll showed Friday. The survey, conducted by Gallup Korea from Tuesday through Thursday on 1,000 people aged 18 and older, showed that positive assessments of Lee's performance gained 1 percentage point from the previous week. Those who disapproved of Lee's handling of state affairs also rose 1 percentage point to 50 percent. Lee's approval rating has fluctuated between 39 and 41 percent for seven weeks since mid-October. Among those who positively assessed Lee's performance, 29 percent cited diplomacy, up from 24 percent the previous week, followed by economic and livelihood issues at 10 percent, and communication at 5 percent. results.title: Korean mystery thriller 'White Blast' set for English-language remake
results.content: Korean mystery thriller "White Blast" is heading for a global audience, with an English-language remake officially confirmed and original director Hong Eui-jeong set to return behind the camera. The film, which continues to attract strong audience interest and critical praise in Korea, follows a mysterious death at a remote rural railway station cut off by heavy snowfall. As retirement approaches, veteran stationmaster Gap-soo (Kim Yoon-seok) finds himself caught up in an unsettling mystery alongside his newly appointed successor, Hyun-taek (Koo Kyo-hwan). The Canadian production company Rhombus Media will co-produce the remake with the original film’s production company, Lewis Pictures. results.title: Police raid justice ministry, prosecution over alleged records leak to lawmaker
results.content: Police on Friday raided the justice ministry and prosecution offices over allegations that investigative records were leaked to independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency sent investigators to search the ministry, the Supreme Prosecutors Office and the Seoul Western District Prosecutors Office and secure evidence related to the allegations. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea filed a complaint against Han in September on suspicion of disclosing official secrets after he raised lobbying allegations against then Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won. Han at the time unveiled a prosecution report about Kim's lobbying allegations, drawing questions over how he obtained the document. Kim later withdrew his candidacy amid growing controversy over the scandal.

results.title: North Korea's Kim urges grassroots party leaders to faithfully relay directives
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has urged the party's grassroots leaders to carry its directives faithfully to the people and set an example for the masses, state media reported Friday. Kim made the remarks the previous day during a photo session with participants of the Seventh Conference of Cell Secretaries of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. Cells are the party's most elementary units, with five to 30 members each. The conference ran Tuesday and Wednesday, and discussed ways to meet the policy goals set at the ninth party congress in February, which laid out five-year targets for sectors, including the economy and defense. Praising the grassroots leaders' devotion, the North's leader told them to do more to rally the masses and put party policy into practice. results.title: North Korean troops cross inter-Korean border about 40 times over past 2 months: lawmaker
results.content: North Korean troops have crossed the heavily fortified inter-Korean border on roughly 40 occasions over the past two months, a South Korean lawmaker said Friday, following September's mine blast in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean soldiers. The North violated the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) about 30 times in October and roughly 10 times this month, according to data submitted to Rep. Yu Yong-weon of the main opposition People Power Party. North Korean soldiers' border crossing has continued even after the Sept. 21 explosion of North Korea-planted mines south of the DMZ. Pyongyang has denied responsibility. Pyongyang has reinforced border fortification work by installing barbed-wire fences and land mines along the inter-Korean border. results.title: Korea to co-chair vice finance ministers meeting of ASEAN+3 next year
results.content: Seoul's finance ministry said Friday that the country will co-chair the meeting of vice finance ministers and deputy central bankers of Korea, China, Japan and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next year. The Ministry of Economy and Finance said the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies' Meeting will be held in Singapore in April and then in Seoul around November. Korea proposed to discuss financial stability amid the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) as next year's key agenda. Meanwhile, this year's meeting was held in Kyoto, Japan, on Wednesday and Thursday to discuss ways to strengthen regional financial cooperation. results.title: 2 Korean naval submarines under repair after accidents
results.content: Two of the Korean Navy's attack submarines are undergoing repairs after sustaining damage in separate accidents, military officials said Friday. One 1,800-ton Son Won Il-class submarine suffered damage to its protective hull coating after getting entangled in discarded fishing nets during a nighttime mission in the Yellow Sea in September, according to Navy officials. No casualties were reported. With its navigational systems intact, the vessel was able to return to its home port under its own power, the Navy said, adding that it is currently undergoing maintenance and repairs for restoration. Another submarine of the same class, the Hong Beom Do vessel, caught fire in April while undergoing a scheduled overhaul at a shipyard in the southeastern city of Ulsan, about 300 kilometers southeast of Seoul. results.title: Why China is hesitating to send new pandas to Korea
results.content: Chinese Ambassador to Korea Dai Bing said Thursday that Beijing would find it difficult to approve Korea’s request for a pair of giant pandas for a zoo in Gwangju. He cited public backlash in China after the Gwangju Biennale allowed an exhibition to be called “Taiwan Pavilion.” Dai made the remarks during a press conference in central Seoul, following China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. "Pandas are China's national treasure and China has relevant laws and regulations on the protection of rare animals. Any loan must go through strict procedures in accordance with these regulations. More than 40 pandas are currently on loan to countries outside China," Dai said. results.title: Seoul stocks up over 2% Friday morning amid AI jitters
results.content: South Korean stocks traded sharply higher late Friday morning, extending a tentative recovery after a volatile week, led by gains in technology shares amid continued market jitters over artificial intelligence (AI). After opening 0.37 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its earlier gains to trade up 105.42 points, or 2.24 percent, to 4,816.63 as of 11:20 a.m. Investors are watching whether the tech rally has staying power after days of volatility driven by doubts over the sustainability of the AI trade. Overnight, Wall Street was closed for the Thanksgiving holiday. In Seoul, large-cap shares were trading higher across the board.
